synthesis.description: Gas control or a connected pipeline announces planned maintenance, pigging, tie-ins, turbine work or an unplanned leak repair. Logistics staff identify the meters in the affected section, notify the desk and producers or customers whose meters will be shut in or curtailed, and arrange how the gas is handled: holding it and batching it later, rescheduling, or deciding what to do when an outage is postponed. Some rounds need a notification letter to shippers.
steps: Gas control or a connected pipeline announces planned or emergency work on a section, plant or station.
Staff identify the meters in the affected section, checking the list against the pipeline's records.
The desk and affected producers or customers are notified of the shut-in or reduced capacity and its dates.
Counterparties agree how volumes are handled, such as holding gas and batching it later.
Notification letters are drafted where shippers must be formally informed.
Updates on postponements or extended outages are passed along until the work is complete.
synthesis.approach: A reusable maintenance notice that takes the section, dates and affected meter list from the pipeline's records and goes to a standing distribution of the desk and affected producers and customers, with fields for expected volume impact, the handling arrangement and any postponement update.
synthesis.rationale: Most rounds are the same announcement re-sent with a new meter list and dates; a standard notice with the meter list drawn from the system cuts the retyping and makes postponements easy to reissue, while staff still agree how volumes are handled.
